history.summary: Per legend, the Sabara chief Biswabasu worshipped the deity as 'Kitung' in a cave in the Brahmadri hills. The Puranas say the deity was originally an Indranila gem image called Nilamadhava; King Indradyumna's quest for it (via his priest Vidyapati) led to the discovery of the sacred daru log and the founding of the Jagannath cult at Puri - so Kantilo is regarded as the original/precursor abode of Lord Jagannath. The temple stands on the right bank of the Mahanadi near the confluence of the Mahanadi, Kuanria and Kusumi rivers (called the triveni sangam of Odisha), built in Kalinga style like a miniature Puri Jagannath temple, and includes a Siddheswar Shiva shrine and the perennial Brahma Kunda spring within the complex.

name: Nilamadhaba Temple, Kantilo
town_description: Kantilo is a historic town in Nayagarh district, Odisha, on the right bank of the Mahanadi river near its confluence with the Kuanria and Kusumi rivers. It is a noted pilgrimage centre because of the Nilamadhaba Temple, sometimes called the second Jagannath Puri, and a local craft hub for brass and bell-metal work.
